title: When a Black Overspreading Cloud
description: When a Black Overspreading Cloud in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 83, “Thunder”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When a black o-ver-spread-ing cloud Has dark-'ned all the air; And peals of thun-der roar-ing loud Pro-claim the tem-pest near.

lines: And peals of thunder roaring loud
Then guilt and fear, the fruits of sin,
A louder storm is heard within,
The law a fiery language speaks,
Like Satan, who his ruin seeks,
But when the sky serene appears,
He soon forgets his vows and fears,
But whither shall the sinner flee,
The pond'rous earth, and air, and sea,
Will sinners bear to see his face,
Lord, let thy mercy find a way
That they may never hear thee say,
Should be to you a welcome voice,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
